findings.title: Different pages share the same title
findings.evidence: 8 of 30 sampled pages share 2 repeated title(s), e.g. "Bombas 200 Million Items Donated: BeeBetter".
findings.mechanism: The title is how a page is named in a citation and is one of the strongest topic signals a retrieval system has. Identical titles make pages indistinguishable to it, so they compete with one another and the most relevant one is not reliably chosen.

suggested_action.summary: Give every page a unique title describing that page's specific subject.
how: Derive the first part from the page's own H1 or product/article name, never from the site name alone.
platform_specific: Edit the title and description templates in `theme.liquid` and set per-product values in the admin's search-listing preview.
suggested_action.verify: Re-run check ANS-003 and confirm it no longer fires.

findings.title: Pricing pages contain no readable price
findings.evidence: 7 of 7 sampled pricing/product pages contain no numeric price in their text, e.g. https://bombas.com/products/gift-card.
findings.mechanism: Cost is among the most common things asked about any commercial brand. With no number on the page, an assistant cannot answer from the brand's own site and turns to resellers, review sites and forums - sources that are often out of date and never in the brand's control. Publishing a figure is what makes the brand's own page the citable one.

suggested_action.summary: Publish a real figure or an indicative range, even where final pricing is negotiated.
how: State a starting price, a typical range, or a worked example: "from 4,500 GBP per unit per year".
Put it in body text, not in an image or a downloadable PDF.
Mirror it in Offer/AggregateOffer structured data with price and priceCurrency.
If pricing genuinely cannot be published, state what it depends on in plain text - that is still an extractable, quotable answer, where silence is not.
suggested_action.verify: Re-run check ANS-006 and confirm it no longer fires.

findings.title: The site does not answer comparison, use-case or how-to questions
findings.evidence: Across 30 known URLs there are no pages matching comparison, faq, how_to, use_case patterns; only none present.
findings.mechanism: A large share of the questions put to assistants are comparative or qualifying - which tool for this job, how does this compare to that, is this suitable for my situation. A site that only describes its own products in its own vocabulary has no passage that matches those questions, so the answer is assembled from review sites and competitors' comparison pages instead.

suggested_action.summary: Publish comparison, use-case and how-to pages in the customer's own words.
how: Write honest comparison pages against the alternatives buyers genuinely evaluate, including where the alternative is the better fit - even-handed pages are cited more often than promotional ones.
Publish `for <audience>` or `for <industry>` pages describing the specific situation each serves.
Add how-to and getting-started content answering the questions that precede a purchase decision.
Title and phrase each page as the question it answers.
suggested_action.verify: Re-run check ANS-009 and confirm it no longer fires.
